title: Gravitational Waves in Geometric–Information Cosmological Evolution: Transition Sources, Continuous Frequency Bands, and Inter-Epoch Transfer — Conditional Mechanisms, Energy Transfer, and Formal Proof Sources
content: Within the derivative-coupled effective action shared with the three-epoch model, we analyze the neutral, symmetric, shift-symmetric background branch and derive \(X\propto a^{-6}\), the mass zero-crossing slope \(\alpha=-\dot m_{\rm eff}^{\,2}(t_c)=6H_c|b|\), and the instability band \(p/a<\mu=\sqrt{-b-\gamma X}\). We construct transverse-traceless (TT) sources from non-collinear scalar gradients and show that, within the stated approximation, each tensor wavenumber \(0<K<2\mu\) admits a nonzero two-mode source. In the short-time constant-coefficient model of single real mode, zero initial data, no post-source impulse, a finite-duration exponential source leaves strictly positive residual wave energy. These results establish a conditional radiation mechanism and a continuous frequency band, but do not select a unique spectral peak; the companion contains conditional proof bodies. At the neutral origin, the composite branch of the neutrino-condensation model shares the instability structure through \(b_N=(G_0^{-1}-C)/Z_m\) and \(\gamma_N=\eta/Z_m\); a conserved nonzero time-charge branch cannot originate from an exactly vanishing condensate and requires a separate perturbation analysis. The present-day frequency is \(f_0=(a_*/a_0)K_*/(2\pi\hbar)\). For radiation domination with an adiabatic benchmark, \(f_0\simeq2.6493\times10^{-8}\,q_*(T_*/\mathrm{GeV})\,\mathrm{Hz}\), where \(q_*=K_*/H_*\) must be computed from the source. Emission before reheating also depends on the pre-reheating expansion and entropy history. The three cosmological epochs provide, respectively, early statistical and background conditions, possible intermediate-era inhomogeneous sources, and late-time propagation under conditional vacuum domination; their number fixes neither the number of emission events nor the number of spectral peaks. We derive a composite-parameter upper band bound, an explicit Gaussian spatial UETC with independent temporal coherence, and a tensor-work energy budget. Continuous-time covariance and finite-wave-packet positivity complement the earlier single-mode result. We formulate a unified unequal-time-correlator (UETC) and Green-function response framework, audit the legacy frequency estimates, and exhibit explicit examples of frequency non-uniqueness. The companion Lean file formalizes selected parts of this evidence chain under explicit assumptions; the physical matching, source statistics, and thermal history remain to be determined.
